# latentclasscausal

R interface to the Julia package **LatentClassCausal.jl**: causal
inference **for latent class and latent profile models**. Latent classes
are patterns across several indicators, so the usual causal toolkit does
not say how a treatment moves people between classes, for whom an
intervention on some indicators matters, or whether the latent pattern
itself confounds an effect. The package answers these questions about
latent classes:

| Question about latent classes | Function |
|:---|:---|
| Does a treatment change **latent class membership**? Δₖ = P(C(1) = k) − P(C(0) = k) | [`intervene_membership()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_membership.md) |
| Does an intervention on exposures change membership in a **latent class outcome**? | [`intervene_latent_outcome()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_latent_outcome.md) |
| **For whom?** How large is the effect within each latent class of the exposures? | [`intervene_within()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_within.md) |
| Could the **latent class itself confound** the effect, and how strongly would it have to? | [`intervene_latent_sensitivity()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_latent_sensitivity.md) |
| **Unmeasured confounding** of treatment and class membership: how strong would it have to be? | [`intervene_membership_sensitivity()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_membership_sensitivity.md) (E-values, additive bias) |
| **Measurement non-invariance** by treatment (DIF)? | [`intervene_dif()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_dif.md) |
| **Heterogeneity** across observed subgroups: Δₖ within a subgroup | [`intervene_subgroup()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_subgroup.md) |
| Adjust for the **latent pattern** of the other exposures instead of each one | `intervene_effect(adjust = "classes")` |
| How would the class model **classify** the post-intervention profiles? (descriptive) | [`intervene_shares()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_shares.md) |

Underneath,
[`intervene_effect()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_effect.md)
provides the estimators these methods build on — the parametric
g-formula, IPTW, AIPW and TMLE for static
([`setto()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/natural.md)),
stochastic
([`shift()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/natural.md)),
targeted
([`subgroup()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervention.md))
and natural-course interventions on binary exposures — and can be used
on its own for an observed outcome.

The package builds on
[latentmixtures](https://github.com/williamlorder/latentmixtures), which
fits the measurement models
([`lca()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/latentmixtures/man/lca.html),
[`lpa()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/latentmixtures/man/lpa.html)), and uses
the same Julia process.

## Installation

You need Julia ≥ 1.12 (for example installed with
[juliaup](https://github.com/JuliaLang/juliaup)) on the `PATH`, or
`JULIA_BINDIR` pointing to its `bin` directory.

\
`# R packages (latentmixtures first); the repositories are private: set GITHUB_PAT first`\
[`install.packages`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/install.packages.html)`(`[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"JuliaConnectoR"``, ``"rlang"``, ``"tidyselect"``, ``"generics"``, ``"remotes"``)``)`\
`remotes``::`[`install_github`](https://remotes.r-lib.org/reference/install_github.html)`(``"williamlorder/latentmixtures"``)`\
`remotes``::`[`install_github`](https://remotes.r-lib.org/reference/install_github.html)`(``"williamlorder/latentclasscausal"``)`\
\
`# Julia packages LatentMixtures.jl and LatentClassCausal.jl into the default Julia environment`\
`latentmixtures``::`[`install_julia_packages`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/latentmixtures/man/install_julia_packages.html)`(``causal_url ``=`` ``"https://github.com/williamlorder/LatentClassCausal.jl"``)`\
`# or from local copies:`\
`# latentmixtures::install_julia_packages(path = "path/to/LatentMixtures.jl",`\
`#                                        causal_path = "path/to/LatentClassCausal.jl")`

The repositories are private: you need read access, and Git must be able
to authenticate to github.com (for example `gh auth login` followed by
`gh auth setup-git`, or a personal access token in your Git credential
helper).

Documentation:
<https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/>.

## The Julia session

All computation runs in **one** Julia process per R session, managed by
latentmixtures. Fitting a model starts it if needed; latentclasscausal
loads LatentClassCausal.jl into that same process the first time you
call one of its functions, and loads it again if the session has been
restarted. To choose the number of threads, start the session yourself
before the first fit:

\
`latentmixtures``::`[`lm_start`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/latentmixtures/man/lm_start.html)`(``threads ``=`` ``8``)``   ``# or set JULIA_NUM_THREADS before starting R`\
`# ... work ...`\
`latentmixtures``::`[`lm_end`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/latentmixtures/man/lm_start.html)`(``)``                ``# fitted models cannot be used after this`

(If your latentmixtures version has no
[`lm_start()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/latentmixtures/man/lm_start.html),
set `JULIA_NUM_THREADS` before the first call.)

## 1. Treatment effects on latent classes: `intervene_membership()`

The package ships two simulated datasets with known true effects
([`?programme`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/programme.md),
[`?ace_study`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/ace_study.md)).
`programme`: 2,000 students, participation in a school mental-health
programme (`programme`, 0/1), five baseline confounders and eight
wellbeing items six months later that measure three latent classes
(Flourishing, Moderate, Distressed).

\
[`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(``latentmixtures``)`\
[`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(``latentclasscausal``)`\
[`data`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/data.html)`(``programme``)`\
\
`# Does the programme move students into the Flourishing class?`\
`m`` ``<-`` ``programme`` ``|>`` `[`lca`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/latentmixtures/man/lca.html)`(``low_mood``:``friends``, K ``=`` ``3``)``   ``# measurement model, items only`\
[`convergence`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/latentmixtures/man/convergence.html)`(``m``)``         ``# check that the best LL is replicated and EM reached the maximum`\
\
`r`` ``<-`` `[`intervene_membership`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_membership.md)`(``m``, ``programme``, treatment ``=`` ``programme``,`\
`                confounders ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``female``, ``age``, ``low_ses``, ``distress``, ``belonging``)``)`\
`r``                      ``# Δ ≈ +0.196, −0.055, −0.141 (true +0.18, −0.06, −0.12)`\
[`tidy`](https://generics.r-lib.org/reference/tidy.html)`(``r``)``                ``# one row per class: estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high, psi1, psi0, ...`\
[`glance`](https://generics.r-lib.org/reference/glance.html)`(``r``)``              ``# N, estimator, entropy, propensity range`\
[`intervene_membership`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_membership.md)`(``m``, ``programme``, treatment ``=`` ``programme``, estimator ``=`` ``"naive"``)``   ``# ≈ 0: confounded`

The data must contain the rows the model was fitted to, in the same
order. The call also works with the data piped in first
(`programme |> intervene_membership(m, treatment = programme, confounders = c(age, female))`)
or with vectors
(`intervene_membership(m, treatment = a, confounders = X)`). Factor
confounders are dummy-coded.

Options: `estimator = "aipw"` (default), `"ipw_bch"`, `"or"` (three-step
ML outcome regression), `"ipw_modal"`, `"aipw_posterior"` or `"naive"`;
`propensity_model` and `outcome_model` (`"linear"` or `"quadratic"`);
`folds` (cross-fitting, default 5); `trim` (propensity truncation).

### What you have to assume

- **No unmeasured confounding of treatment and class.** Given the
  confounders, who gets treated is unrelated to which class people would
  be in under each treatment level (conditional exchangeability), and
  everyone has some chance of each treatment level (positivity).
- **Measurement invariance.** The latent classes mean the same thing for
  treated and untreated people and at every value of the confounders:
  given the class, the indicator response probabilities (or profile
  means) do not depend on the treatment or the confounders. In other
  words, the treatment and the confounders act on the indicators only
  through the latent class. This is what allows a measurement model
  fitted without covariates to be reused. If treatment changes how
  people answer an item directly (differential item functioning), Δₖ is
  biased. Check this, for example by fitting multigroup models across
  treatment groups or testing direct effects of the treatment on the
  indicators.
- **A well-fitting measurement model** with the right number of classes.
  Standard errors account for estimating the model but not for choosing
  K.
- Double robustness: with the default AIPW estimator it is enough for
  **either** the propensity model **or** the latent class regression on
  treatment and confounders to be correctly specified.

## 2. Latent classes and interventions on exposures

Childhood adversities co-occur in patterns that latent class analysis
reads as a latent family context, but an intervention targets specific
adversities. These functions connect the two; the running example
prevents abuse and neglect (`ace1`, `ace2`) in `ace_study` (eight
adversities, three latent classes, outcome past-year depression).

\
[`data`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/data.html)`(``ace_study``)`\
`# For whom? Effect within each adversity class (posterior-weighted; bootstrap SEs refit the LCA)`\
`ce`` ``<-`` `[`intervene_within`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_within.md)`(``ace_study``, outcome ``=`` ``depressed``, exposures ``=`` ``ace1``:``ace8``, intervene ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``ace1``, ``ace2``)``,`\
`                    confounders ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``age``, ``female``, ``parent_edu``)``, g1 ``=`` `[`setto`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/natural.md)`(`[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``0``, ``0``)``)``, K ``=`` ``3``,`\
`                    family ``=`` ``"binomial"``)`\
`ce``                   ``# risk difference ≈ −0.210 in the high-adversity class, ≈ −0.009 in the low one`\
`# How would the class model classify the post-intervention profiles? (descriptive)`\
`sh`` ``<-`` `[`intervene_shares`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_shares.md)`(``ace_study``, exposures ``=`` ``ace1``:``ace8``, intervene ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``ace1``, ``ace2``)``,`\
`                   confounders ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``age``, ``female``, ``parent_edu``)``, g1 ``=`` `[`setto`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/natural.md)`(`[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``0``, ``0``)``)``, K ``=`` ``3``)`\
`# Could a direct effect of the latent family context explain the effect away?`\
[`intervene_latent_sensitivity`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_latent_sensitivity.md)`(``ace_study``, outcome ``=`` ``depressed``, exposures ``=`` ``ace1``:``ace8``, intervene ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``ace1``, ``ace2``)``,`\
`                   confounders ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``age``, ``female``, ``parent_edu``)``, g1 ``=`` `[`setto`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/natural.md)`(`[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``0``, ``0``)``)``, K ``=`` ``3``,`\
`                   target ``=`` `[`which.max`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/which.min.html)`(``sh``$``pi0`` ``-`` ``sh``$``pi1``)``, family ``=`` ``"binomial"``)`\
`# Adjust for the latent pattern of the other adversities instead of each one`\
[`intervene_effect`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_effect.md)`(``ace_study``, outcome ``=`` ``depressed``, exposures ``=`` ``ace1``:``ace8``, intervene ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``ace1``, ``ace2``)``,`\
`                    confounders ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``age``, ``female``, ``parent_edu``)``, g1 ``=`` `[`setto`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/natural.md)`(`[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``0``, ``0``)``)``,`\
`                    family ``=`` ``"binomial"``, adjust ``=`` ``"classes"``, adjust_K ``=`` ``3``)`\
`# A latent class outcome: does the programme change membership in wellbeing classes?`\
[`data`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/data.html)`(``programme``)`\
`mo`` ``<-`` ``latentmixtures``::`[`lca`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/latentmixtures/man/lca.html)`(``programme``, ``low_mood``:``friends``, K ``=`` ``3``)`\
[`intervene_latent_outcome`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_latent_outcome.md)`(``mo``, ``programme``, exposures ``=`` ``programme``, intervene ``=`` ``programme``,`\
`                          confounders ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``female``, ``age``, ``low_ses``, ``distress``, ``belonging``)``,`\
`                          g1 ``=`` `[`setto`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/natural.md)`(``1``)``, g0 ``=`` `[`setto`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/natural.md)`(``0``)``)`

The vignette
([`vignette("latentclasscausal")`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/articles/latentclasscausal.md),
section 2) explains each research question, the assumptions (in
particular no direct effect of the class beyond the exposures, which
[`intervene_latent_sensitivity()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_latent_sensitivity.md)
probes) and the status of each method.

## 3. The intervention estimators underneath: `intervene_effect()`

`ace_study`: 2,500 adults, eight adverse childhood experiences (`ace1`
abuse, `ace2` neglect, … `ace8`), confounders `age`, `female`,
`parent_edu` and two outcomes, self-rated health (`health`, 0–100) and
past-year depression (`depressed`, 0/1).

\
[`data`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/data.html)`(``ace_study``)`\
\
`# Would preventing childhood abuse and neglect (ace1, ace2) improve adult health?`\
`ie`` ``<-`` ``ace_study`` ``|>`\
`  `[`intervene_effect`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_effect.md)`(``outcome ``=`` ``health``, exposures ``=`` ``ace1``:``ace8``, intervene ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``ace1``, ``ace2``)``,`\
`                      confounders ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``age``, ``female``, ``parent_edu``)``, g1 ``=`` `[`setto`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/natural.md)`(`[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``0``, ``0``)``)``,`\
`                      estimator ``=`` ``"tmle"``)`\
`ie``                     ``# ψ ≈ +2.265 points (true +2.00)`\
[`tidy`](https://generics.r-lib.org/reference/tidy.html)`(``ie``)``               ``# rows: E[Y^g1], E[Y^g0], effect`\
\
`# halve the prevalence of abuse and neglect; risk difference for depression`\
[`intervene_effect`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_effect.md)`(``ace_study``, ``depressed``, ``ace1``:``ace8``, `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``ace1``, ``ace2``)``, `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``age``, ``female``, ``parent_edu``)``,`\
`                    g1 ``=`` `[`shift`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/natural.md)`(``0.5``)``, family ``=`` ``"binomial"``)``   ``# ψ ≈ −0.0205 (true −0.021)`\
\
`# prevent abuse only, neglect unchanged; and prevention targeted at families with low`\
`# parental education`\
[`intervene_effect`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_effect.md)`(``ace_study``, ``health``, ``ace1``:``ace8``, `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``ace1``, ``ace2``)``, `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``age``, ``female``, ``parent_edu``)``,`\
`                    g1 ``=`` `[`intervention`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervention.md)`(``function``(``s``, ``a``)`` `[`as.numeric`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/numeric.html)`(`[`all`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/all.html)`(``s`` ``==`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``0``, ``a``[``2``]``)``)``)``,`\
`                                      label ``=`` ``"prevent abuse only"``)``)`\
[`intervene_effect`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_effect.md)`(``ace_study``, ``health``, ``ace1``:``ace8``, `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``ace1``, ``ace2``)``, `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``age``, ``female``, ``parent_edu``)``,`\
`                    g1 ``=`` `[`subgroup`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervention.md)`(`[`setto`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/natural.md)`(`[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``0``, ``0``)``)``, ``parent_edu`` ``<=`` ``10``)``)`\
\
`# compare two static interventions instead of the natural course`\
[`intervene_effect`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_effect.md)`(``ace_study``, ``health``, ``ace1``:``ace8``, ``ace1``, `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``age``, ``female``, ``parent_edu``)``,`\
`                    g1 ``=`` `[`setto`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/natural.md)`(``0``)``, g0 ``=`` `[`setto`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/natural.md)`(``1``)``)`

`intervene` is selected among `exposures`, in the order written, which
is the order of the values in
[`setto()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/natural.md).
Rows with missing values are dropped (with a message). Use
`family = "binomial"` for a 0/1 outcome (ψ is then a risk difference).
The working models are set with `outcome_model` and `propensity_model`,
and `folds` controls cross-fitting.
`intervention_effect_matrix(y, exposures, X, S, g1)` is the same
function for vectors and matrices.

### What you have to assume

- **Exchangeability.** Given the other exposures and the confounders,
  the intervened exposures are as good as randomly assigned: there is no
  unmeasured common cause of them and the outcome.
- **No latent confounding.** This is the critical assumption when the
  exposures are indicators of a latent class. If the latent variable
  that produces the indicators (for example a general “adverse
  environment”) also affects the outcome directly, adjusting for the
  other indicators controls for it only partly (proxy adjustment) and ψ
  is biased. The estimate answers “what if we removed this exposure,
  holding the person’s other exposures as they are”, not “what if we
  changed the latent class”.
- **The intervened exposures do not cause the other exposures**
  (otherwise the other exposures are mediators, and adjusting for them
  blocks part of the effect).
- **Positivity.** People with every combination of other exposures and
  confounders must have a real chance of the post-intervention exposure
  values. The printout reports the smallest such probability and the
  largest weight, and warns when overlap is poor.
- **Consistency.** The intervention is well defined: removing an
  exposure by the hypothetical intervention has the same effect as not
  having had it.

AIPW and TMLE are doubly robust: they are consistent if either the
outcome model or the model for the intervened exposures is correctly
specified. The g-formula relies on the outcome model alone (bootstrap
standard errors), and IPTW on the exposure model alone.

## 4. Sensitivity analyses

Each method rests on an assumption the data cannot check; each has a
sensitivity or diagnostic tool:

| Threat | Applies to | Tool | What it reports |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Unmeasured confounding of treatment and class | [`intervene_membership()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_membership.md) | [`intervene_membership_sensitivity()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_membership_sensitivity.md) | per class, E-values for the causal risk ratio P(C(1)=k)/P(C(0)=k) (VanderWeele & Ding 2017) and tipping points of an additive bias model (biases sum to zero over classes) |
| Measurement non-invariance by treatment (DIF), which invalidates the BCH correction | [`intervene_membership()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_membership.md) | [`intervene_dif()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_dif.md) | scaled χ² test of invariant vs treatment-specific measurement (multigroup LCA) and Δₖ with treatment-specific classification errors |
| The latent class of the exposures affects the outcome directly (latent confounding) | [`intervene_effect()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_effect.md), [`intervene_within()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_within.md) | [`intervene_latent_sensitivity()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_latent_sensitivity.md) | tipping points of the direct class effect γ at which the effect vanishes or its interval includes 0 |
| Extreme weights from rare exposure profiles | [`intervene_effect()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_effect.md) | `adjust = "classes"` / `"both"` | the effect with the other exposures summarised by their latent class |
| Heterogeneity across observed subgroups | [`intervene_membership()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_membership.md) | [`intervene_subgroup()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_subgroup.md) | Δₖ within a subgroup |

\
`s`` ``<-`` `[`intervene_membership_sensitivity`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_membership_sensitivity.md)`(``m``, ``programme``, treatment ``=`` ``programme``,`\
`                     confounders ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``female``, ``age``, ``low_ses``, ``distress``, ``belonging``)``, target ``=`` ``1``)`\
`s``                      ``# E-values and tipping points for the Flourishing class`\
[`autoplot`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/autoplot.html)`(``s``)`\
[`intervene_dif`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_dif.md)`(``m``, ``programme``, indicators ``=`` ``low_mood``:``friends``, treatment ``=`` ``programme``,`\
`        confounders ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``female``, ``age``, ``low_ses``, ``distress``, ``belonging``)``)``   ``# DIF by treatment?`\
`# latent confounding for interventions on exposures: see intervene_latent_sensitivity() in section 2`

## Machine-learning nuisance models

Both estimators also accept flexible working models. `propensity_model`
and `outcome_model` can be `"lasso"`, `"lasso_quadratic"`,
`"elasticnet"`, `"ridge"`, `"forest"`, `"boost"` (needs the Julia
package EvoTrees.jl) or `"superlearner"`, and `learners` sets the super
learner’s library. Learners are fitted only within the cross-fitting
training folds, and propensities from learners are bounded to
`[bound, 1 - bound]`:

\
[`intervene_membership`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_membership.md)`(``m``, ``programme``, treatment ``=`` ``programme``, confounders ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``female``, ``age``, ``low_ses``, ``distress``, ``belonging``)``,`\
`           propensity_model ``=`` ``"superlearner"``, outcome_model ``=`` ``"superlearner"``)`\
[`intervene_effect`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_effect.md)`(``ace_study``, outcome ``=`` ``health``, exposures ``=`` ``ace1``:``ace8``, intervene ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``ace1``, ``ace2``)``,`\
`                    confounders ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``age``, ``female``, ``parent_edu``)``, g1 ``=`` `[`setto`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/natural.md)`(`[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``0``, ``0``)``)``,`\
`                    outcome_model ``=`` ``"superlearner"``, propensity_model ``=`` ``"lasso_quadratic"``,`\
`                    learners ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"glm"``, ``"lasso_quadratic"``, ``"forest"``)``)`

The *Machine-learning nuisance models* page of the LatentClassCausal.jl
documentation gives the details and a Kang–Schafer simulation.

## Tables

[`lm_table()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/latentmixtures/man/lm_table.html)
(the table generic of latentmixtures) and
[`causal_table()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/causal_table.md)
produce stargazer-style tables with stars and standard errors, in text,
Markdown, LaTeX (booktabs) or HTML. Results of both kinds can be
combined, and named arguments become column headings:

\
[`lm_table`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/latentmixtures/man/lm_table.html)`(``` `Programme`  ```=`` ``r``` , `ACE 1-2 = 0`  ```=`` ``ie``)``                       ``# console`\
[`lm_table`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/latentmixtures/man/lm_table.html)`(``r``, format ``=`` ``"latex"``, file ``=`` ``"tab_lcc.tex"``, title ``=`` ``"Effect on class membership"``)`\
`ie_aipw`` ``<-`` `[`intervene_effect`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_effect.md)`(``ace_study``, ``health``, ``ace1``:``ace8``, `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``ace1``, ``ace2``)``,`\
`                               `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``age``, ``female``, ``parent_edu``)``, g1 ``=`` `[`setto`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/natural.md)`(`[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``0``, ``0``)``)``)`\
[`causal_table`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/causal_table.md)`(``AIPW ``=`` ``ie_aipw``, TMLE ``=`` ``ie``, format ``=`` ``"markdown"``, ci ``=`` ``TRUE``)`

[`causal_table()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/causal_table.md)
works with any version of latentmixtures. When latentmixtures exports
[`lm_table()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/latentmixtures/man/lm_table.html),
[`lm_tab()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/latentmixtures/man/lm_tab.html) and
[`lm_render()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/latentmixtures/man/lm_tab.html), the
[`lm_table()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/latentmixtures/man/lm_table.html)
methods are registered automatically and tables are drawn by
latentmixtures’ renderer, so they match the tables of that package.

## Plots

[`autoplot()`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/autoplot.html)
(ggplot2) and [`plot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/plot.default.html)
methods draw the standard figures from the stored results, and
[`causal_plot()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/causal_plot.md)
compares several results; all return ggplot objects and use the theme
and colour-blind-safe palette of latentmixtures.

\
[`autoplot`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/autoplot.html)`(``r``)``                          ``# forest plot of the class effects`\
[`autoplot`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/autoplot.html)`(``r``, type ``=`` ``"probabilities"``)``  ``# P(C(1) = k) vs P(C(0) = k)`\
[`autoplot`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/autoplot.html)`(``r``, type ``=`` ``"overlap"``)``        ``# propensity-score overlap by treatment group`\
[`autoplot`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/autoplot.html)`(``ie``)``                         ``# E[Y^g1], E[Y^g0] and their difference`\
[`autoplot`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/autoplot.html)`(``ie``, type ``=`` ``"overlap"``)``       ``# propensity of each intervened exposure pattern`\
[`autoplot`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/autoplot.html)`(``ie``, type ``=`` ``"weights"``)``       ``# inverse-probability weights`\
`ie_gf`` ``<-`` `[`intervene_effect`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/intervene_effect.md)`(``ace_study``, ``health``, ``ace1``:``ace8``, `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``ace1``, ``ace2``)``,`\
`                             `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``age``, ``female``, ``parent_edu``)``, g1 ``=`` `[`setto`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/natural.md)`(`[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``0``, ``0``)``)``,`\
`                             estimator ``=`` ``"gformula"``)`\
[`causal_plot`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/causal_plot.md)`(``AIPW ``=`` ``ie_aipw``, TMLE ``=`` ``ie``` , `g-formula`  ```=`` ``ie_gf``, what ``=`` ``"all"``)`

## Function overview

| Function | Purpose |
|----|----|
| `intervene_membership(model, data, treatment, confounders, ...)` | effect of a binary treatment on latent class membership |
| `intervene_effect(data, outcome, exposures, intervene, confounders, g1, g0, ...)` | effect of interventions on binary exposures |
| `intervention_effect_matrix(y, exposures, X, S, g1, g0, ...)` | matrix interface of the above |
| [`natural()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/natural.md), `setto(values)`, `shift(delta, from, to)` | interventions |
| `intervention(rule)`, `subgroup(g, condition)` | custom and subgroup interventions |
| [`lcc_available()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/lcc_available.md) | is Julia with LatentClassCausal.jl installed? (guards examples) |
| [`tidy()`](https://generics.r-lib.org/reference/tidy.html), [`glance()`](https://generics.r-lib.org/reference/glance.html), [`as.data.frame()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/as.data.frame.html), [`coef()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/coef.html), [`nobs()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/nobs.html) | results as data frames / vectors |
| [`causal_table()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/causal_table.md), [`lm_table()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/latentmixtures/man/lm_table.html) | publication tables |
| [`autoplot()`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/autoplot.html), [`plot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/plot.default.html), [`causal_plot()`](https://williamlorder.github.io/software/latentclasscausal/reference/causal_plot.md) | figures (ggplot2) |

Printing uses UTF-8 symbols (Δ, ψ, box rules) when the locale supports
them; set `options(latentclasscausal.ascii = TRUE)` for plain ASCII.

## Further reading

The Julia package documents the estimators in detail:
`LatentClassCausal.jl/docs/theory.md` (identification, BCH
pseudo-outcomes, influence functions) and `docs/interventions.md`
(g-formula, IPTW, AIPW, TMLE for static and stochastic interventions).
